question: Which of the following refers to "A hypothetical region of space from which nothing, not even light, can escape"?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Black Hole**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Black Hole"** refers to a region in space where the gravitational pull is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from it. (अंतरिक्ष में एक ऐसा क्षेत्र जहां से प्रकाश भी नहीं निकल सकता)
 
 
• **Example:** Scientists use advanced telescopes to study the properties of black holes in distant galaxies.
 
 
• A black hole is formed when a massive star collapses under its own gravity, creating a singularity with infinite density and zero volume. (ब्लैक होल तब बनता है जब कोई विशाल तारा अपने ही गुरुत्व के कारण संकुचित हो जाता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Black Hole**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Wormhole** (वर्महोल): A hypothetical tunnel-like structure in space-time, which could connect two distant points in space or time.
 
 
• **Example:** Wormholes are often depicted in science fiction as shortcuts for space travel.
 
 
 
• **Singularity** (विशिष्टता): A point in space-time where gravitational forces cause matter to have infinite density and zero volume.
 
 
• **Example:** The center of a black hole is known as a singularity.
 
 
 
• **Event Horizon** (घटना क्षितिज): The boundary surrounding a black hole beyond which nothing can escape.
 
 
• **Example:** The event horizon marks the point of no return around a black hole.
